title: 13.5 An 18.5µW/qubit Cryo-CMOS Charge-Readout IC Demonstrating QAM Multiplexing for Spin Qubits
problem: Scaling spin qubits to thousands of devices requires simultaneous readout with minimal per-qubit power consumption and footprint, but existing FDM reflectometry and integrator schemes are limited by bulky inductors or poor scaling to large arrays.
motivation: Spin qubits offer promise for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing with small footprint (<1µm²) and higher operating temperatures, but simultaneous readout of thousands of devices within thermal constraints is the critical challenge.
method: The chip measures the charge state of multiple spin qubits simultaneously using a single radio-frequency carrier wave, with QAM multiplexing (encoding different signals by varying the wave's amplitude and phase) allowing each qubit's signal to be distinguished on the same frequency. This approach shares the RF generation and amplification resources across multiple qubits, reducing per-qubit power consumption compared to designs that need a separate carrier for each qubit. Instead of the bulky inductors (coils) that earlier readout designs used, this circuit achieves amplification through a capacitive-feedback architecture (which couples signals through a capacitor), saving chip area and power; the result is 18.5 microwatts per qubit operating in CMOS at cryogenic temperatures.
key_novelty: This design enables reading multiple spin qubits using a single radio-frequency carrier with QAM multiplexing (varying amplitude and phase), instead of requiring one carrier per qubit like earlier on-off-keying schemes.
contributions: Demonstrated 18.5µW/qubit power consumption meeting cryo-thermal constraints
QAM multiplexing increases readout bandwidth efficiency vs OOK
Inductor-less FDM architecture using capacitive-feedback transimpedance amplifier
Scalability pathway to thousands of qubits in large arrays
primary_theme: scalable cryo-CMOS spin qubit readout with QAM multiplexing
